import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.41

by P. M. Neumann

Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$ define a *$k$-section* of $\Omega$
to be a partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets.

b) Does there exist a group that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on $(k+1)$-sections?

c) Does there exist a transitive permutation group on $\Omega$ that is transitive on
$\aleph_0$-sections but which is a proper subgroup of $\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$?

Here "group" means a permutation group $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, and $G$ is transitive on
$k$-sections if the induced action of $G$ on the set of all $k$-sections of $\Omega$ has a
single orbit.

Only part b) is formalised in this file. For part c), a positive answer is consistent with the
ZFC axioms of set theory (S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, 2025).

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 9.41
- [S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, *A permutation group acting transitively on certain collections of
  models*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12997)
-/

open Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«9.41»

variable {Ω : Type*}

/--
A *$k$-section* of $\Omega$ is a partition of $\Omega$ as a union of $k$ infinite sets.
It is recorded as an (unordered) set $c$ of subsets of $\Omega$ which is a partition of
$\Omega$, has exactly $k$ elements, and all of whose elements are infinite.
-/
def IsSection (k : ℕ) (c : Set (Set Ω)) : Prop :=
  Setoid.IsPartition c ∧ c.encard = k ∧ ∀ b ∈ c, b.Infinite

/--
A permutation group $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ is *transitive on $k$-sections* if the induced
action of $G$ on the set of all $k$-sections of $\Omega$ has a single orbit: for any two
$k$-sections $P$ and $Q$ there is $g \in G$ with $g P = Q$, where
$g P = \{g(B) \mid B \in P\}$.
-/
def IsTransitiveOnSections (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P Q : Set (Set Ω), IsSection k P → IsSection k Q → ∃ g ∈ G, g • P = Q

/-- A $k$-section has finitely many blocks. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsSection.finite {k : ℕ} {c : Set (Set Ω)} (hc : IsSection k c) : c.Finite :=
  Set.finite_of_encard_eq_coe hc.2.1

/-- There are no $0$-sections of a nonempty set. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem not_isSection_zero [Nonempty Ω] (c : Set (Set Ω)) : ¬ IsSection 0 c := by
  rintro ⟨⟨-, hc⟩, hcard, -⟩
  rw [Nat.cast_zero, Set.encard_eq_zero] at hcard
  obtain ⟨b, ⟨hb, -⟩, -⟩ := hc (Classical.arbitrary Ω)
  simp [hcard] at hb

/-- Transitivity on $k$-sections is inherited by overgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsTransitiveOnSections.mono {G H : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)} (hGH : G ≤ H) {k : ℕ}
    (hG : IsTransitiveOnSections G k) : IsTransitiveOnSections H k := by
  intro P Q hP hQ
  obtain ⟨g, hg, hgP⟩ := hG P Q hP hQ
  exact ⟨g, hGH hg, hgP⟩

/--
Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$ a $k$-section of $\Omega$ is a
partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets. Does there exist a group that is
transitive on $k$-sections but not on $(k+1)$-sections?

Here "group" means a permutation group $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, the same group $G$
is considered for $k$-sections and $(k+1)$-sections, and the question is asked for every
$k \geq 2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.41».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (Ω : Type) [Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω], ∀ k ≥ 2,
      ∃ G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω),
        IsTransitiveOnSections G k ∧ ¬ IsTransitiveOnSections G (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.41»
attempts.decomposition_objections: Part c) was dropped as having 'no statable Prop', but it appears statable: `∃ G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω), G ≠ ⊤ ∧ MulAction.IsPretransitive G Ω ∧ (transitive on ℵ₀-sections)`, where an ℵ₀-section is a partition into countably infinitely many infinite blocks (`c.Infinite` in place of `c.encard = k`). The ZFC question remains open (Corson–Shelah 2025 only prove consistency under MA(σ-centered)), so it could be stated as `research open` with `answer(sorry)`. I conformed to the table and did not formalize it.
modeling_decisions: Ω is quantified universally over all countably infinite types (`∀ (Ω : Type) [Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω]`) rather than fixed to ℕ; the two are equivalent since the property is invariant under bijections of Ω.
Following the decomposition notes, the implicit quantifier on k is read as 'for every k ≥ 2 there exists G' (∀ k ≥ 2, ∃ G ...), with the same G for the k- and (k+1)-section conditions.
'Group' is modelled as `Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)`; an abstract group acting (possibly unfaithfully) on Ω would give an equivalent statement via its image in Sym(Ω).
k-sections are unordered (sets of blocks), as in the notes; blocks of a partition are automatically distinct so `c.encard = k` counts blocks correctly.
G is not required to be transitive on Ω in part b) (the statement only imposes that in part c)).

Three short `@[category API]` lemmas (finiteness of the block set, no 0-sections on nonempty Ω, monotonicity of transitivity in G) are included as basic API tests of the bespoke definitions; all are proved.

new_definitions.name: Kourovka.«9.41».IsSection

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.41

by P. M. Neumann

Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$, a $k$-section of
$\Omega$ is a partition of $\Omega$ into $k$ infinite sets. Does there exist a
permutation group on $\Omega$ that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on
$(k+1)$-sections?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.41»

/-- A $k$-section of $\Omega$ is an unordered partition of $\Omega$ into exactly
$k$ infinite blocks. -/
def IsKSection {Ω : Type*} (k : ℕ) (P : Partition (Set.univ : Set Ω)) : Prop :=
  (P : Set (Set Ω)).Finite ∧ (P : Set (Set Ω)).ncard = k ∧
    ∀ B ∈ P, B.Infinite

/-- A permutation group is transitive on the $k$-sections of $\Omega$ if any
such section can be mapped to any other by an element of the group. -/
def IsTransitiveOnSections {Ω : Type*} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P Q : Partition (Set.univ : Set Ω), IsKSection k P → IsKSection k Q →
    ∃ g : G, {g.1 '' B | B ∈ P} = (Q : Set (Set Ω))

/--
For every $k \geq 2$, does there exist a permutation group on a countably
infinite set $\Omega$ that is transitive on the unordered partitions of
$\Omega$ into $k$ infinite blocks, but is not transitive on the unordered
partitions into $k+1$ infinite blocks?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.41».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (Ω : Type) [Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω] (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k →
      ∃ G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω),
        IsTransitiveOnSections G k ∧ ¬ IsTransitiveOnSections G (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.41»
modeling_decisions: A countably infinite set Ω is represented by a type with both `Countable Ω` and `Infinite Ω`.

A k-section is represented using Mathlib's `Partition (Set.univ : Set Ω)`, whose blocks are unordered, nonempty, pairwise disjoint, and cover Ω; the added predicate requires the block family to be finite of `ncard` k and every block to be infinite.

A permutation group is a `Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)`. Transitivity is stated directly: for every pair of k-sections, an element of the subgroup maps the unordered set of blocks of the first exactly to that of the second.

Following the fixed decomposition, the implicit quantifier on k is formalized universally for every k ≥ 2, with the subgroup allowed to depend on k; the same subgroup is used for k-sections and (k+1)-sections.

/-!

by P. M. Neumann

$\Omega$ is a partition of $\Omega$ into $k$ infinite sets. Problem 9.41(b)
asks whether, for every such $k$, there is a permutation group on $\Omega$
that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on $(k+1)$-sections.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.41»

/-- A $k$-section of $\Omega$ is an unordered partition of $\Omega$ into exactly
$k$ infinite blocks. -/
def KSection (Ω : Type*) (k : ℕ) :=
  {P : Set (Set Ω) //
    Setoid.IsPartition P ∧ Nat.card P = k ∧ ∀ B ∈ P, B.Infinite}

/-- A permutation group is transitive on the $k$-sections of $\Omega$ if every
$k$-section can be carried to every other one by an element of the group. -/
def IsTransitiveOnSections {Ω : Type*} (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ P Q : KSection Ω k, ∃ g : G,
    (fun B : Set Ω => (g : Equiv.Perm Ω) '' B) '' P.1 = Q.1

/--
For every integer $k \geq 2$, does there exist a permutation group
$G \leq \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ that is transitive on the unordered
partitions of the countably infinite set $\Omega$ into $k$ infinite blocks,
but is not transitive on its unordered partitions into $k+1$ infinite blocks?
The same group $G$ is used in both actions.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.41».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (Ω : Type) [Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω] (k : ℕ), 2 ≤ k →
      ∃ G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω),
        IsTransitiveOnSections G k ∧ ¬ IsTransitiveOnSections G (k + 1) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.41»
modeling_decisions: A countably infinite set is represented by a type with both `Countable` and `Infinite` instances.
The implicit quantifier on k is formalized universally: for every natural k with `2 ≤ k`, the required subgroup may depend on k and on Ω.
A permutation group on Ω is represented faithfully as `Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)`.

Sections are unordered set partitions. Transitivity is stated directly by requiring a group element whose pointwise images of all blocks of one section form exactly the other section; this avoids choosing labels for blocks.
`Nat.card P = k` counts the subtype of blocks. Since the theorem only uses k ≥ 2 (and k + 1), this equality also rules out an infinite collection of blocks, for which `Nat.card` is zero.

For every $k \geq 2$, does there exist a permutation group on the countably infinite set
$\Omega$ that is transitive on the unordered partitions of $\Omega$ into $k$ infinite blocks,
but is not transitive on the unordered partitions of $\Omega$ into $k+1$ infinite blocks?

A partition is represented by a setoid on $\Omega$. Its blocks are the elements of the quotient,
and a permutation sends one partition to another when it preserves and reflects the corresponding

theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔

      let IsTransitive := fun (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) n ↦
        ∀ s t, IsSection n s → IsSection n t →
          ∃ g : G, ∀ x y, s.r x y ↔ t.r (g.1 x) (g.1 y)

        IsTransitive G k ∧ ¬IsTransitive G (k + 1) := by
  sorry

Represented a permutation group on Ω as `Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)` and stated transitivity directly by requiring a group element that transports either section relation to the other.
Quantified over every countably infinite type Ω and every natural number k with 2 ≤ k, matching the arbitrary Ω in the preamble and the decomposition table's implicit universal quantifier on k.

/-!
# Conjecture 9.41

by P. M. Neumann

Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$ define a *$k$-section* of
$\Omega$ to be a partition of $\Omega$ as union of $k$ infinite sets.

b) Does there exist a group that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on
$(k + 1)$-sections?

Here a "group" is a permutation group $G \leq \mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$, acting on
$k$-sections by moving the blocks, and $G$ is *transitive on $k$-sections* if this
induced action on the set of all $k$-sections has a single orbit. The quantifier on
$k$ is implicit: the question is asked for every $k \geq 2$, with the same group $G$
acting on $k$-sections and on $(k+1)$-sections.

The notebook also contains a part c), asking for a transitive proper subgroup of
$\mathrm{Sym}(\Omega)$ that is transitive on $\aleph_0$-sections. A positive answer
to c) is consistent with ZFC (Corson–Shelah, 2025). Part c) is not formalised here.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 9.41
- [S. M. Corson, S. Shelah, *A permutation group acting transitively on certain
  collections of models*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12997)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«9.41»

variable {Ω : Type*}

/-- A `k`-section of `Ω` is a partition of `Ω` into exactly `k` infinite sets. It is
recorded as the (unordered) set `c` of its blocks: `c` is a partition of `Ω`, it has
exactly `k` blocks, and every block is infinite. -/
def IsSection (k : ℕ) (c : Set (Set Ω)) : Prop :=
  Setoid.IsPartition c ∧ c.encard = k ∧ ∀ s ∈ c, s.Infinite

/-- A permutation group `G ≤ Sym(Ω)` is transitive on `k`-sections if for any two
`k`-sections `c` and `d` there is some `g ∈ G` with `g • c = d`, where `Sym(Ω)` acts on
sets of subsets of `Ω` pointwise, i.e. `g • c = {g '' s | s ∈ c}`. -/
def IsTransitiveOnSections (G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c d : Set (Set Ω), IsSection k c → IsSection k d → ∃ g ∈ G, g • c = d

/-- The action of `Sym(Ω)` on sets of subsets of `Ω` used in `IsTransitiveOnSections`
moves each block `s` of `c` to its image `g '' s`. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem smul_set_set_eq_image (g : Equiv.Perm Ω) (c : Set (Set Ω)) :
    g • c = (fun s => g '' s) '' c := by
  rfl

/-- The blocks of a `k`-section are nonempty. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsSection.nonempty {k : ℕ} {c : Set (Set Ω)} (hc : IsSection k c) {s : Set Ω}
    (hs : s ∈ c) : s.Nonempty :=
  (hc.2.2 s hs).nonempty

/-- The even and odd natural numbers form a `2`-section of `ℕ`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isSection_even_odd : IsSection 2 {{n : ℕ | Even n}, {n : ℕ | Odd n}} := by
  have hne : {n : ℕ | Even n} ≠ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := by
    intro h
    have : (0 : ℕ) ∈ {n : ℕ | Odd n} := h ▸ Even.zero

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.41

by P. M. Neumann

Let $\Omega$ be a countably infinite set. For $k \geq 2$, a $k$-section of $\Omega$ is a
partition of $\Omega$ into $k$ infinite sets. Does there exist, for every $k \geq 2$, a
permutation group on $\Omega$ that is transitive on $k$-sections but not on
$(k+1)$-sections?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«9.41»

open scoped Pointwise

variable {Ω : Type*} [Countable Ω] [Infinite Ω]

/--
For every integer $k \geq 2$, does there exist a permutation group $G \leq
\operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ whose induced action is transitive on the unordered partitions of
$\Omega$ into exactly $k$ infinite blocks, but whose induced action is not transitive on the
unordered partitions into exactly $k+1$ infinite blocks?

Here `Setoid.IsPartition P` says that `P` is an unordered partition of $\Omega$, and the
pointwise action `g • P` applies the permutation `g` to every block of `P`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k →
      ∃ G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω),
        (∀ P Q : Set (Set Ω),
          Setoid.IsPartition P ∧ P.ncard = k ∧ (∀ B ∈ P, B.Infinite) →
          Setoid.IsPartition Q ∧ Q.ncard = k ∧ (∀ B ∈ Q, B.Infinite) →
          ∃ g : G, g • P = Q) ∧
        ¬(∀ P Q : Set (Set Ω),
          Setoid.IsPartition P ∧ P.ncard = k + 1 ∧ (∀ B ∈ P, B.Infinite) →
          Setoid.IsPartition Q ∧ Q.ncard = k + 1 ∧ (∀ B ∈ Q, B.Infinite) →
          ∃ g : G, g • P = Q) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.41»
modeling_decisions: The countably infinite set Ω is represented by an arbitrary type with `Countable Ω` and `Infinite Ω` instances.
A k-section is represented as an unordered family `P : Set (Set Ω)` satisfying Mathlib's `Setoid.IsPartition P`, with `P.ncard = k` and every member of `P` infinite.

A permutation group is represented as `G : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm Ω)`. Its induced action on sections is the nested pointwise action; `g • P` applies `g` to every element of every block and to the resulting family of blocks.
Transitivity is stated directly as: for every two qualifying sections P and Q, some `g : G` sends P to Q. Non-transitivity on `(k+1)`-sections is the negation of this same condition for the same G.
The implicit quantifier in part b is read, as required by the decomposition, as `∀ k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → ∃ G, ...`.
